findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: The facility uses both quaternary ammonia (wipes) and chlorine bleach (triple sink) to sanitize food contact surfaces. The facility still does not did not have a test kit for chlorine bleach, and the test kit for the quaternary ammonia was observed to have expired 7/1/24. Obtain new test strips for both sanitizers. All chemical sanitizing solutions used for food contact surfaces must have a test kit to verify the concentration recommended by the manufacturer’s label.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed an accumulation of biofilm on the front and back of the ice machine baffles. A new follow up inspection is scheduled for 7/1/26 to verify compliance. Empty, clean, and sanitize the ice machine. Ensure all food contact surfaces are maintained clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events.
findings.comment: The person in charge (PIC) was unable to provide written procedures for cleanup of vomit or diarrhea. CORRECTED- inspector provided CDC Norovirus cleanup handout to the PIC. Ensure these directions are either kept on file or posted so that staff may follow proper disinfection procedures to prevent the potential spread of Norovirus.
findings.citation_text: 2-501.11 Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events. A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. [Pf]

Empty, clean, and sanitize the ice machine. Ensure all food contact surfaces are maintained clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the gaskets of the standing cooler to contain an accumulation of debris. Ensure nonfood contain surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris, which may contaminate foods of food contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple items in the physical facility in need of repair.
1) SECOND REPEAT: The wall in the kitchen is missing caulking behind the rinse and wash portions of the triple sink. Ensure the sink is resealed to the wall to allow for a smooth, easily cleanable surface.
2) SECOND REPEAT: The backsplash of the sink in the women’s restroom is bare wood. Paint or seal the bare wood so that it is smooth and easily cleanable.
3) FIRST REPEAT: A gap exists between the mop sink and the wall directly to the left. Re-adhere the sink basin to the wall to prevent the entry and harborage of mold.
4) The wall to the left of the hand washing sink in the men’s restroom contains holes and bare wood, where the previous soap dispenser was located. Fill holes and paint bare wood.
Ensure physical facilities are maintained in proper repair.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: All temperature control for food safety (TCS) food items were observed to be out of temperature in the facility’s prep cooler. Items include, but are not limited to: ham (64F), ham salad (69F), chicken breasts (70F), roast beef (65F), and ham salad (64F). CORRECTED- items that had been in the unit for over 4 hours were voluntarily discarded. Items that had been in the unit for less than 2 hours were either moved to time as control or moved to the working standing cooler. TCS foods must be used or discarded within 4 hours after being removed from temperature control (41F and under for cold holding).
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: The prep cooler was observed to have an ambient temperature of 60F, and is failing to hold TCS foods at temperature- see violation #22. The PIC stated the AC in the building is scheduled to be fixed the following morning, and that will hopefully prevent the unit from over working. A follow up inspection is scheduled for 6/15/26 to verify that the prep cooler is holding TCS foods at or below 41F.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: Inspector observed 2 cans of olives and tomato sauce to be dented along the seams. CORRECTED- the cans were separated from cans from service to be returned to food supplier. Ensure cans are checked for any dents along the seams, and sizable dents along the body when stocking. Dented cans may allow for the entry and growth of Botulism.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. [Pf]

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Inspector observed light entering the facility along the perimeter of the back door. A sizable gap (about 1-2cm) exists in the upper right corner. Ensure the door is repaired by the next routine inspection to protect against the entry of pests.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors. [C]

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed paper plates used for catering service stored with their food contact surface facing upwards in the dry storage. CORRECTED- education about protecting food contact surfaces from potential contamination was provided. The PIC stated they would place the single service articles in a bag. Ensure all food contact surfaces are stored in a position that protects from potential contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor. [C]

2) FIRST REPEAT: The backsplash of the sink in the women’s restroom was bare wood. Paint or seal the bare wood so that it is smooth and easily cleanable.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed an accumulation of black and pink soil on the baffles of the ice machine. CORRECTED- staff member wiped the area with a clean sanitizer cloth. Ensure food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to be clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector observed multiple foods in prep cooler to be out of temperature (chicken salad at 47F, tuna salad at 46F, and shredded lettuce at 50F). Other foods in the cooler were observed between 43-45F. CORRECTED- The out of temperature foods voluntarily discarded by the person in charge (PIC). Other foods were observed at 43-45F or dropped in temperature to below 45F during in the inspection and were moved to another cooler. Monitor food temperatures to ensure foods are held at 41F or below. Keep the prep cooler lid closed as much as possible to aid in maintaining safe food temperatures.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: Foods in the prep cooler were observed between 43-50F. Out of temperature foods were voluntarily discarded while other foods were moved to the storage cooler in the kitchen (see violation #22). The prep cooler was observed with an ambient temperature of 47F, and to contain a small pool of condensation on the bottom left side of the cooler.. Make the necessary adjustments or repairs to the cooler so that foods are held at 41F or below. Continue to monitor the cooler and consider creating cooler temperature logs. Follow up will be conducted to verify the cooler is functioning properly.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Inspector observed food debris on the interior of the prep cooler along the back edge (along the hinge). Education occurred regarding routine cleaning of nonfood contact surfaces. Ensure nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple items in the physical facility in need of repair.
1) The triple sink in the kitchen is missing caulking in multiple areas. Ensure the sink is resealed to the wall to allow for a smooth, easily cleanable surface.
2) The backsplash of the sink in the women’s restroom was bare wood. Paint or seal the bare wood so that it is smooth and easily cleanable.
3) The men’s restroom contains multiple holes in the wall from where the previous soap dispenser was located. Fill in the holes.
Ensure physical facilities are maintained in proper repair.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
REPEAT- Food handler certificates could not be located for an employee who was present during this inspection. Ensure all employees complete food handler training within 30 days of hire and renew as needed. Keep food handler certificates on file in the facility for review during health inspections.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. [C]

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.comment: Signed reporting agreements were not on file for employees present during this inspection. Ensure signed reporting agreements are kept on file for all employees as proof that they have been educated on foodborne illness symptoms and diagnoses that would limit their ability to work in the kitchen. Inspector will follow up in 10 days to see that signed reporting agreements are on file.
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A). [Pf]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Employees were observed moving from the cash register to donning gloves without washing hands first. CORRECTED- Provided education to PIC and employees present. Review handwashing procedures with all employees. Ensure employees wash hands before donning gloves.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD. [P]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: An employee was observed to wash hands then turn the faucet off without using a barrier. CORRECTED- Provided education to employee and PIC. Educate all employees to use a paper towel or other barrier to turn the faucet off after washing hands. This prevents recontamination of newly-cleaned hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [P]

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: 1st REPEAT: The 2 door cooler and prep cooler do not have an ambient thermometer inside. Ensure all cold holding units have ambient thermometers present inside and placed at the warmest part of the cooler.
findings.citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: There is a ceiling tile missing above the mop sink/water heater area. Replace the ceiling tile.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Slight pink & brown mold accumulation was observed on the baffle inside the ice machine. CORRECTED- PIC sanitized the baffle. Continue to clean on a regular basis to prevent soil accumulation.
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
There is no ambient thermometer present in the prep cooler. Ensure all cold holding units have ambient thermometers present inside to monitor the air temperature.
4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. [C]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
Gasket is damaged and falling off of the middle door of the prep cooler. Repair so the gasket is attached and seals door shut.
4-501.11: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications. (C) Cutting or piercing parts of can opens shall be kept sharp to minimize metal fragmentation. [C]

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Raw shell eggs were observed stored above ready-to-eat deli meats in the 2 door cooler. CORRECTED- PIC rearranged storage so that eggs are below all ready-to-eat foods. Review storage to prevent cross contamination with staff.
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display. [P]

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
Facility’s probe thermometer read approx 40F when placed in ice water. CORRECTED- Reviewed thermometer calibration process and calibrated the thermometer so it accurately read 32F in ice water.
4-203.11: (A) FOOD TEMP. MEASURING DEVICE shall be accurate to  +/- 1 Celsius (B) accurate to +/- 2 Fahrenheit. [Pf]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean

6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
No paper towels were available in the womens restroom. CORRECTED- Staff refilled paper towel dispenser.
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [Pf]

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
Lids, paper towels, napkins, and toilet paper observed stored on the floor in the dry storage closet. CORRECTED- Items were rearranged to be stored at least 6” off the ground.
4-903.11: (A) clean EQUIPMENT and clean ARTICLES shall be stored in clean, dry location where they are not exposed to contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean

1) Bare wood is exposed on the back (kitchen side) of the iced tea shelf. Paint to seal bare wood.
2) A two-inch hole was observed behind to the soda syrup rack in the kitchen. Seal hole.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
Gasket is damaged and falling off of the middle door of the prep cooler. Repair so that gasket is attached and seals door shut.
4-501.11: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications. (C) Cutting or piercing parts of can opens shall be kept sharp to minimize metal fragmentation. [C]

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
Opened bottle of frappuccino observed stored on a middle shelf of the 2 door cooler above foods for service. Store personal foods below or away from foods intended for service.
6-501.110: (A) Dressing rooms shall be used by EMPLOYEES if the EMPLOYEES regularly change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions. [C]

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
CFM has not completed allergen awareness training. All CFPMs must complete ANSI approved allergen awareness training. Complete training and keep certificates on file for review during inspections.
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text: 4-602.11 Mold was observed on the ceiling in the ice bin along the walls behind the baffle. Management noted the ice machine was new to the facility and leased by the owners within the last two weeks. Cleaning was discussed. Ensure surfaces that can be reached are cleaned and sanitized between full services. Equipment with enclosed components, such as ice machines, shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Lettuce in the top right holding compartment of the sandwich prep cooler was observed with an internal temperature of 50F. Manager confirmed temperature with the facility’s calibrated stem thermometer. Lettuce was washed and cut around 10am and stacked with other containers in the 2 door cooler prior to storage in the prep cooler for service within the hour prior to inspector’s arrival. All coolers were observed holding below 40F, and other foods in coolers were at proper temperature. Lettuce was in a plastic container and wrapped tightly, so that storage in combination with being stacked may not have allowed for chilling after prep. Lettuce will be served or discarded by 7:30pm.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 Assistant manager has not yet completed the food manager course to obtain certification. An employee with a manager certification was on-site. However, that employee was not the PIC, and their shift concluded before 5pm. Designated PIC at time of inspection plans to complete an online course in the upcoming week and take certification exam at the end of the month.  
 Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an accredited program.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed
findings.citation_text:
5-403.12 Issue with ponding condensation was improved since the previous inspection but not resolved. PIC noted the owners came in to adjust the cooler, which resulted in condensation accumulating at a slower rate. However, ponding condensation is still an issue in the bottom of the cooler. Upon further investigation it would appear the condensing unit has ponding water that may be seeping from the back ledge to the bottom inside the cooler. Moisture was visible along the edge of the shelving on the back ledge, and accumulation of condensation was observed in the cooler on the bottom left side. Owners need to have the prep cooler serviced by a licensed refrigeration technician. **See general comments for additional information**
Condensate drainage and other non-sewage liquids and rainwater shall be drained from point of discharge to disposal according to law.

findings.title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, & cleaned
findings.citation_text:
6-202.14  Women’s restroom door does not self-close flush with the door frame. Provide repairs so the door shuts properly.
All toilet rooms located within a food establishment must be enclosed with a tight-fitting and self-closing door.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 1. Paint was peeling above the women's room handsink. Repaint the wall above the handsink.
2. Floor tiles around the grease trap were damaged. Accumulation of debris was observed, and the area around the grease trap is not smooth/easily cleanable. At minimum, owners need to provide a cleanable cover (hard plastic, solid mat) to cover the area, which will allow for ease in cleaning and help minimize the potential for debris and water accumulation in the area. 
3. Gap was observed at the upper corner where the three part sink meets the wall, and the drain board was not sealed to the wall. Finish sealing the gap in the corner, and seal the 3 part sink to the wall to allow for ease in cleaning. 
4. Gap was observed at the floor to wall juncture in the corner under the 3 part sink. Plastic coving was loose along the top where repairs were attempted. Finish sealing the are under the 3 part sink drain board. 
5. Base coving was loose under the handwashing sink. Re-attach the base coving. 
6. Hole was observed in the wall of the women’s restroom where door handle comes in contact. Repair the wall.
NOTE: Repair and repaint any and all surfaces that are in disrepair throughout the facility.
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.07 PIC needs to complete the online allergen awareness training. Ensure all CFMs also complete the allergen certification. Maintain copies of certification on-site with all other certifications.
Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Bleach solution at 3 part sink was observed at 100ppm. The solution was prepared within the hour prior to inspector’s arrival based on information provided. Solution was discarded. Preparing bleach solutions at proper concentration and use of test strips to verify concentration were discussed. Ensure bleach solutions are maintained at proper concentration of 200ppm as required by product label directions. 
A chlorine solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Poblano & cheese soup was observed with an internal temperature of 113F-115F. Warmer was turned up to a higher setting, and soup was reheated to 175F. Leftover portion of soup will be discarded at the end of operations today.  
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135F/above.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.citation_text:
4-203.11 Food thermometer was observed near 20F at room temperature. Ice point method was used to calibrate the thermometer to 32F, but the built-in adjustment tool was not working consistently. The needle didn’t move at first attempt, and the needle was easily bumped out of place when thermometer was barely touched. A new thermometer was purchased during inspection and calibrated for use.  
Food temperature measuring devices that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±2°F in the intended range of use.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-204-112 Thermometer in the bottom of the prep cooler was submerged in puddling condensation and not working properly. Provide a new thermometer for the prep cooler. 
 Cold holding equipment used for time/temperature  control for safety (TCS) food shall be designed to include and shall be equipped with at least one permanently affixed temperature measuring device that is located to allow easy viewing of the device's temperature display.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 Ponding condensate drainage and food debris were observed throughout the bottom of the prep cooler. Bottom inside the prep cooler should be cleaned as frequently as necessary to minimize the presence of ponding condensate and food debris until cooler is properly repaired to eliminate condensation buildup (see #52 for details).
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.citation_text:
5-205.15 Kitchen handwashing sink faucet has a leak at the base when water is in use. Water splashes up and to the side causing droplets to accumulate on the side of the freezer to the right of the sink when hands are washed. Clean equipment storage is located to the left of the handwashing sink but did not appear to get splashed when the handwashing sink was in use. Provide proper repairs to eliminate splashing water on surfaces adjacent to the sink. 
A plumbing system shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed
findings.citation_text:
5-403.12 A significant amount of ponding condensation was observed in the bottom of the prep cooler. PIC noted the issue began several months ago with a small amount of condensate drainage ponding on the left side, but now condensation buildups throughout the bottom of the cooler. Containers in the bottom of the cooler are in direct contact with dirty condensate drainage, and if not handled properly pose a risk of potential cross contamination on the make line. This is an issue that needs to be resolved immediately. Provide repairs to allow for proper drainage and disposal of condensation.
Condensate drainage and other non-sewage liquids and rainwater shall be drained from point of discharge to disposal according to law.

findings.title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, & cleaned
findings.citation_text:
6-202.14  Women’s restroom door does not self-close flush with the door frame. Provide repairs so the door shuts properly.
All toilet rooms located within a food establishment must be enclosed with a tight-fitting and self-closing door.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 1. Paint was peeling above the women's room handsink. Repaint the wall above the handsink.
2. Floor tiles around the grease trap were damaged. Accumulation of debris was observed, and the area around the grease trap is not smooth/easily cleanable. At minimum, owners need to provide a cleanable cover (hard plastic, solid mat) to cover the area, which will allow for ease in cleaning and help minimize the potential for debris and water accumulation in the area. 
3. Gap was observed at the upper corner where the three part sink meets the wall, and the drain board was not sealed to the wall. Finish sealing the gap in the corner, and seal the 3 part sink to the wall to allow for ease in cleaning. 
4. Gap was observed at the floor to wall juncture in the corner under the 3 part sink, and the floor to wall juncture under the drain board was not properly sealed. Finish sealing the are under the 3 part sink drain board. 
5. Base coving was loose under the handwashing sink. Re-attach the base coving. 
6. Hole was observed in the wall of the women’s restroom where door handle comes in contact. Repair the wall.
NOTE: Repair and repaint any and all surfaces that are in disrepair throughout the facility.
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11 (O) Food employee working with PIC at time of inspection did not have a signed reporting agreement on file. Manager had the employee review and sign the reporting agreement during inspection. Ensure all staff are educated on the employee health policy upon hiring and sign reporting agreements prior to beginning their first shift. Maintain signed copies of reporting agreements for staff.
The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under ¶ 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Employee washed hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off prior to getting paper towels to dry hands. Proper handwashing technique was discussed. Signage that shows the steps of proper handwashing is posted above the kitchen handwashing for reference. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.citation_text:
4-203.11 Food thermometer was checked using ice water method for calibration during inspection. Thermometer was reading near 20F. Thermometer was calibrated to 32F. Ensure frequent calibration of food thermometer for accuracy during temperature checks. 
Food temperature measuring devices that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±2°F in the intended range of use.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.citation_text:
6-202.15 Back door is not self-closing and has to be forced shut to be tight fitting. If allowed to close by itself, the door does not seal flush with the door frame. Repair the back door so it is self-closing and tight fitting. 
Outer openings of food establishments shall be protected against entry of insects and rodents with solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.citation_text:
4-202.16 Handle of the left sliding door on the chest freezer was loose and pulls away from the glass when attempting to open/close the door. Provide proper repairs so the handle stays on and does not pull away from the glass.
Non-food contact surfaces shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 Wall on the left side of the mopsink was in disrepair. The paint has worn off and the wall surface underneath was exposed. Repair the wall and re-seal the mosink to the wall. 
-Three part sink used to be sealed to the wall at the right side along the dirty dish drain board. The seal was gone and general buildup of mold and splash were observed in the crevice. Clean and re-seal the 3 part sink to the wall at the dirty dish drain board. 
-Paint was peeling under the dirty dish drain board. Re-seal the wall under the 3 part sink drain board.
-Wall just above the floor at the corner under the 3 part sink was damaged. A gap was present and the inner wall structure was exposed. Repair and repaint the wall above the floor. 
-Paint was peeling above the women's room handsink. Repaint the wall above the handsink.
-Floor tiles around the grease trap were damaged. Accumulation of water and debris were observed in the crevices around the grease trap lid in the past. At minimum, owners need to provide a cleanable cover (hard plastic, solid mat) to cover the area, which will allow for ease in cleaning and help minimize the potential for debris and water accumulation in the area.
-Wall by the back door had peeling, and the wall surface underneath was exposed. Lower right side by the door frame was also damaged. Provide proper repairs to the wall around the back door. 
-Floor in front service area has an opening in the floor with what appears to be a recessed electrical outlet. Crumbs and debris accumulation were observed, and the area in question is not easily cleanable. Provide a cover. 
NOTE: Repair and repaint any and all surfaces that are in disrepair throughout the facility.
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 Employee working with PIC at time of inspection did not have a food handler certification and has worked at the facility for a little over a month. Ensure all staff that are not certified food managers complete an online food handler certification course within 30 days of hiring, and maintain copies of certifications on-site.
All food handlers, other than someone who has a food manager certification, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 PIC did not have proof of food manager certification at the time of inspection. PIC just passed the test and needs to print a copy of the certification. 
 Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an accredited program.

The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under ¶ 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Knives were soiled with food debris at the sandwich prep cooler. One of the knives was cleaned since lunch service began but the other had not yet been cleaned. Both knives were taken to dish area to be properly cleaned and sanitized. Ensure proper cleaning and sanitizing of knives during operations.
If used with TCS foods equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be cleaned up to every 4hrs throughout the day after continuous use.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Meatballs in hot holding well were observed with internal temperatures at 113F-137F. Meatballs in the bottom of the pan were at 135F/above while meatballs stacked higher were below 135F. Meatballs were heated this morning for lunch, and manager stated meatballs reached an internal temperature of 182F prior to service. Meatballs were initially going to be reheated to 165F. Manager decided to start with fresh product and discarded the meatballs in question. All other foods in the hot holding wells were at proper temperature or were in the process of being heated for service. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135F/above.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.07 PIC needs to complete the online allergen awareness training. Ensure all CFMs also complete the allergen certification. Maintain copies of certification on-site with all other certifications.
Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 PIC did not have proof of food manager certification at the time of inspection. PIC is in the process of completing certification (see general comments for details).
 Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an accredited program.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Employee washed hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off without a barrier, and the handle of the paper towel dispenser was then touched to dispense paper towels to dry hands. Proper handwashing technique was discussed. Signage that shows the steps of proper handwashing is posted above the kitchen handwashing for reference. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Employee was getting ready to stock lids for cups without first washing their hands. Employee was handling soiled dishes prior to getting the sleeve of lids. Employee washed hands at request of inspector. Ensure handwashing occurs between tasks.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles, and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.14 Handwashing signage was not posted in the women's room. Handwashing sign was posted in the bathroom during inspection.
A sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands shall be provided at all handwashing sinks used by food employees and shall be clearly visible to food employees.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 Soda nozzle at Freestyle machine was soiled with slimy mold buildup, and the surface above the nozzle had buildup of splash. Nozzle was cleaned and sanitized during inspection, and the surface above where the nozzle attached was cleaned. Ensure Freestyle machine nozzle, the surface above the nozzle, and the area where the nozzle attaches to the machine are cleaned and sanitized as needed to eliminate buildup of mold and splash.
Food shall only contact surfaces of equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified under Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of the 2017 FDA Food Code.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11 Small mesh baking trays by the oven were soiled with food debris from use the previous operating day. Baking trays were not cleaned and sanitized at the close of operations the day prior. Baking trays were taken to dish area to be cleaned and sanitized prior to use. 
Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be clean to sight and touch. Ensure baking trays are getting cleaned ad sanitized daily.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-202.12 Bleach solution used to wipe down tables was observed at a concentration well above 200ppm. The test strip was bleached out by the solution. PIC diluted the solution to be at 200ppm. Ensure staff are trained on use of test strips to verify concentration of bleach solutions, and maintain solutions at 200ppm per manufacturer's instructions for use. 
Chemical sanitizers must meet the concentration and use requirements specified by 40 CFR 180.940. Toxics shall be used according to the manufacturer's use directions included in labeling, and must not be used in a manner that poses a health hazard or potential risk of cross contamination.

Food temperature measuring devices that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±2°F in the intended range of use.
